title: AT&T Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates as Fiber Adds Hit a Record; 2026 Outlook Raised
excerpt: Adjusted EPS of $0.65 topped the $0.61 consensus on revenue of $32.32 billion; a $2.6 billion Mexico impairment cut reported EPS to $0.13.
body:
• AT&T's third-quarter adjusted EPS rose 20.4% to $0.65, beating the $0.61 consensus, as revenue grew 5.3% to $32.32 billion against expectations of $31.68 billion.
  • The company added a record 769,000 internet connections in the quarter — 442,000 fiber and 327,000 fixed wireless — plus 379,000 postpaid phone subscribers at 0.92% churn.
  • Reported EPS fell to $0.13 after a $2.6 billion non-cash impairment on the Mexico wireless business being sold; the year-ago quarter's $1.29 included a gain on the DIRECTV stake sale.
  • AT&T raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS outlook to about $2.40 and still expects free cash flow of at least $18 billion.

AT&T beat Wall Street expectations for the third quarter, as record fiber and fixed-wireless additions and steady wireless growth outweighed a large one-time charge on the Mexico business it is selling. The results, released before the market opened on Wednesday, prompted the company to raise its full-year earnings outlook.

Adjusted earnings per share came in at $0.65, up 20.4% from $0.54 a year earlier and ahead of the $0.61 consensus estimate, according to Zacks. Revenue rose 5.3% to $32.32 billion, beating the $31.68 billion analysts had expected. Adjusted EBITDA increased to $12.5 billion, and free cash flow was about $5.0 billion, up slightly from a year earlier.

A Record Quarter for Internet Additions

The standout number was customer growth. AT&T's Advanced Connectivity unit added a record 769,000 internet connections in the quarter — 442,000 fiber and 327,000 fixed wireless — the second consecutive quarter with more than 1 million total advanced-connectivity additions. Postpaid phone net additions were 379,000, ahead of estimates, with churn flat at 0.92%.

Advanced Connectivity revenue rose 7.2% to $29.48 billion, with service revenue up 6.1% to $23.9 billion and segment operating income up 18.9% to $7.6 billion. Wireless service revenue grew 5% to $17.76 billion, helped by subscriber growth and pricing, while consumer home internet revenue jumped 23.4% to $2.98 billion, partly reflecting the mass-market fiber business acquired from Lumen earlier this year. Some 42.8% of AT&T home internet households now also take its wireless service — the converged base the company is counting on for retention.

Why Reported Profit Fell

On a reported basis, diluted EPS from continuing operations dropped to $0.13 from $1.29 a year earlier. The gap to the adjusted figure is explained by a $2.6 billion non-cash impairment on the Mexico wireless unit, which AT&T has agreed to sell to Grupo Televisa and Fintech Holdings, plus employee separation charges. The year-ago quarter also included a gain on the sale of AT&T's DIRECTV investment, flattering the comparison. Operating income was $4.1 billion reported, or $7.6 billion adjusted.

Outlook Raised

AT&T raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS outlook to approximately $2.40, from a prior $2.25–$2.35 range, and maintained its target of at least $18 billion in free cash flow this year. The company said its fiber network now reaches more than 39 million consumer and business locations, on track for over 40 million by the end of 2026 and more than 60 million by the end of 2030. It also lowered its long-term capital investment plans to $22–23 billion a year for 2027 and 2028 and reiterated plans to return more than $45 billion to shareholders across 2026–2028 through dividends and buybacks. Net debt rose sequentially to $149.8 billion after the EchoStar spectrum transaction closed. Despite the beat and the raised outlook, the shares fell about 5.5% in premarket trading, according to GuruFocus.
